note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Arkansas's parties nominate in the March 3 primary and March 31 runoff (Libertarians by convention, Feb 20-22); city offices, judges, prosecutors, school boards and water boards are printed without a party. No Arkansas party page that a program may read calls anything an endorsement for a 2026 state or local race, so 'endorsements' is empty. Under 'other_support', with the page's own wording in 'kind' and never to be shown as an endorsement: the Libertarian Party of Arkansas's '2026 Libertarian Candidates' (its convention nominees), the Republican Party of Arkansas's undated 'State Constitutional Office Republican Candidates' (the Treasurer only), and the Washington County Democrats' 'Current Washington County Democratic Candidates'. Every one of these candidates is on the ballot under that party's own label, so a line adds nothing to the party printed on the ballot; no party page read names a candidate for a judge, city, school or water board contest as its own. Names keep the page's spelling in 'as_listed' (Mark Foster for Mark S. Foster, Dana Deree for Dana D. Deree, Suki Highers for Suki Lin Highers, and names given without the title the ballot name carries, such as Fred Love for State Senator Fred Love). Federal lines on these pages are outside this file. Read on 2026-10-03 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt checked first; every page in 'lists' was opened a second time and a line kept only if the page still showed it. Contact details on the Libertarian page were never stored. Things for a person to decide: whether John opens the Democratic Party of Arkansas's site in his own browser (see not_read), and whether the Libertarian page's 'Hunter Jackson' (House 48) is the ballot's Orion Jackson.

not_read.why: the site answers programs with a CAPTCHA page (SiteGround's, even for robots.txt), so it was left alone. A third-party voter guide found by search (not a party page, not opened) describes the state party as endorsing 2026 legislative candidates; John can open the party's own site in his own browser and save the page if it says so

read (home, candidates, constitutional, Senate and House candidate pages, press releases, news, county committees). Its 'State Senate Republican Candidates' and 'State House of Representatives Republican Candidates' pages are the 2024 lists (Senate District 1 shows Ben Gilmore; the 2026 Senate 1 contest is between Harrell Wilson and Tomeka Butler), so nothing was taken from them. No page says the party endorses anyone for a 2026 state or local race; its candidates page sends readers to the county clerks for local candidates. The county committees page names chairs and meeting places only (not recorded)
